title: Why oil jumped after a tanker was mined

outro.text: Next test: November 3, the US midterm elections. Full story in our deep dive, linked below.

scenes.hook_card: Oil just hit a six-month high. A tanker bomb did it.
scenes.text: Oil just hit a six month high. Brent crude settled at 117 dollars 64 a barrel on Friday.
That's up 13.6 percent in October alone, the fourth monthly gain in a row.

The trigger looked small. A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by limpet mines, explosives stuck to the hull by a small boat. It was the first successful strike like that since the war began in February.

scenes.sticker: One fifth of the world's oil and gas
scenes.text: Hormuz is the sea route for about one fifth of the world's oil and gas.
Here's the strange part. Saudi Arabia's crude exports actually rose in October, according to ship trackers. So barrels are still moving.
So why the jump? Traders aren't pricing today's barrels. They're pricing what comes next. President Trump has signalled he may restart strikes on Iran after the midterms.
An Oxford energy lecturer and veteran oil trader put it bluntly.

quote.text: The market is doing exactly what it is supposed to do: It is telling us there is plenty of prompt oil, but there is no end to this war in sight

scenes.text: And a peace deal may not bring the old prices back. Saxo Bank expects crude at 70 to 90 dollars even after the war ends, up from 60 to 70 before it.
